reason: The bone window has spaces for mineral, and strengthening the bones is one of the goals.
expectation: The mineral should strengthen the living bone framework.

alternatives.reason: The cells also appear ready to build a muscle between the front attachments.

effect: The bones are strengthened with mineral, while the joint remains movable. Next I can build the muscles.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and the movable joint is helpful.
reason: The front attachments have an empty space for muscle cells, as the chapter describes.
expectation: The cells should build a muscle on the front of the elbow.

alternatives.reason: The back attachments also need a muscle; either side could come first.

effect: The front cells formed a biceps that pulls to bend the elbow; the back attachment still needs a muscle.
reaction: The picture makes the connection between the attachment and bending clearer.
reason: The back attachments are the remaining empty muscle-building area.
expectation: The cells should form a muscle behind the elbow that pulls in the opposite direction.

effect: The triceps straightens the elbow using the same kind of pulling cells as the biceps; their different attachments determine the direction. All goals are complete.
reaction: Seeing the two muscles pull in opposite directions made their jobs clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the biceps and triceps was most worthwhile because their placement showed how pulling can bend or straighten the same joint.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second muscle placement felt a little repetitive, although the different result made the comparison useful.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells can produce opposite movements because of where the muscles attach.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary: the pictures showed spaces for mineral and muscle cells.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing familiar body parts assembled and connected to their jobs was understandable and satisfying.
